Manslaughter is recklessly causing the death of another person and is a second-degree felony. Criminally negligent homicide, causing death through criminal negligence, is a state jail felony. The difference turns on the person's mental state: whether they consciously disregarded a substantial risk or failed to perceive it.

These cases often arise from accidents, firearms mishandling, or vehicle collisions. Expert analysis and careful attention to the facts can mean the difference between a felony conviction and a dismissal or reduced charge.

---

## Murder & Homicide
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/violent-crimes/murder/

Murder and capital murder defense in Houston and Fort Bend County from a trial-tested family of firms.

Murder under Penal Code § 19.02 is a first-degree felony punishable by five to ninety-nine years or life. If the jury finds the defendant acted under the immediate influence of sudden passion arising from adequate cause, the punishment drops to the second-degree range. Capital murder, which includes killings of peace officers, multiple victims, or murder during certain felonies, carries life without parole or the death penalty.

Homicide investigations begin long before an arrest, and early representation can influence whether a grand jury indicts. Our affiliated family firm has obtained no-bills in two murder investigations and the dismissal of a capital murder charge. We retain investigators and forensic experts, examine self-defense, and prepare every case for trial.

---

## Houston & Fort Bend Domestic Violence Lawyer
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/domestic-family-violence/

Houston and Fort Bend County domestic violence lawyer: family violence assault, strangulation, protective orders and bond conditions. Call (832) 979-0882.

Family violence charges reach far beyond the courtroom. An arrest can come with an emergency protective order that removes you from your home, bond conditions that bar contact with your partner or children, and a lifetime federal firearm prohibition if you are convicted.

Texas defines family violence broadly to include spouses, former spouses, people who share a child, relatives, people living in the same household, and dating partners. In Harris and Fort Bend Counties, prosecutors handle these cases through specialized units and often proceed even when the complaining witness does not want the case to continue.

The Pink family of firms has obtained dismissals in numerous family violence cases, including a felony charge for impeding breath and a combined burglary and family violence case.

---

## Domestic Assault
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/domestic-family-violence/domestic-assault/

Family violence assault charges in Harris and Fort Bend County: penalties, enhancements and long-term consequences.

Assault causing bodily injury to a family or household member or dating partner is a Class A misdemeanor for a first offense. It becomes a third-degree felony if you have a prior family violence conviction or if the State alleges impeding breath or circulation.

## Consequences Beyond the Sentence
- An "affirmative finding" of family violence follows you and enhances future charges.
- A conviction triggers a federal firearm prohibition.
- Deferred adjudication for family violence cannot be sealed by nondisclosure.
- The case can affect custody, immigration status, and professional licenses.

That is why the goal in most cases is dismissal, acquittal, or a resolution that avoids a family violence finding.

---

## Assault by Strangulation
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/domestic-family-violence/assault-by-strangulation/

Impeding breath or circulation (strangulation) charges in Texas: third-degree felony defense.

Assault by impeding the normal breathing or circulation of the blood, by applying pressure to the throat or neck or blocking the nose or mouth, is a third-degree felony when committed against a family member, household member, or dating partner, even without any prior record.

These allegations are often made during a heated argument with little physical evidence. We scrutinize photographs, medical findings, the complaining witness's statements over time, and any 911 recording. Our affiliated family firm has obtained the dismissal of a felony impeding-breath charge.

---

## Continuous Family Violence
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/domestic-family-violence/continuous-family-violence/

Continuous violence against the family charges in Texas: what the State must prove.

Continuous violence against the family under Penal Code § 25.11 applies when a person commits two or more family violence assaults within a 12-month period. It is a third-degree felony, and the alleged assaults do not need to have resulted in convictions or even arrests.

Because the State can rely on prior incidents that were never charged, we investigate each alleged event separately and challenge vague or unsupported claims.

---

## Interference With an Emergency Call
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/domestic-family-violence/interference-with-emergency-call/

Interference with an emergency request for assistance charges in Texas.

Knowingly preventing or interfering with another person's ability to place an emergency call, or request help from a law enforcement agency, medical facility, or family member, when that person reasonably believes they are in danger, is a Class A misdemeanor. It becomes a state jail felony with a prior conviction.

This charge is often added to family violence arrests. It requires proof that the person was trying to call for help and that the interference was knowing, both of which are often disputed.

---

## Protective Order Hearings
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/domestic-family-violence/protective-order-hearings/

Protective order hearings in Harris and Fort Bend County: emergency orders, final orders and defending your rights.

There are two main types of protective orders. A magistrate's order of emergency protection is often issued automatically at a family violence arrest and can last 31 to 61 days, or up to 91 days if a weapon was involved. A protective order under the Family Code requires a hearing and can last up to two years, and longer in serious cases.

A protective order can remove you from your home, restrict contact with your children, and prohibit you from possessing firearms. Anything you say at the hearing can be used in the criminal case. We represent clients at these hearings to protect both their rights and their criminal defense.

---

## Violation of a Protective Order
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/domestic-family-violence/violation-of-protective-order/

Violation of protective order and bond conditions charges in Houston and Fort Bend County.

Violating a protective order or family violence bond condition, such as communicating with the protected person, going near their home or workplace, or possessing a firearm, is a Class A misdemeanor. It becomes a third-degree felony with two prior violations or if the violation involves an assault or stalking.

Contact initiated by the protected person is still a violation for the restrained person, which surprises many clients. If you have questions about what your order allows, ask us before acting.

---

## Dismissing a Family Violence Charge
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/domestic-family-violence/dismissing-a-family-violence-charge/

How family violence charges get dismissed in Houston, even when the complaining witness wants to drop charges.

Only the prosecutor can dismiss a criminal case. A complaining witness cannot "drop the charges," although their wishes and an affidavit of non-prosecution are often considered. In Harris and Fort Bend Counties, prosecutors may try to proceed using 911 recordings, body-camera video, photographs, and officer testimony.

Many of those pieces of evidence are hearsay that can be excluded unless an exception applies, and the Confrontation Clause limits the use of testimonial statements when the witness does not testify. We build the case for dismissal through investigation, motions practice, and trial preparation.

---

## Women Charged With Domestic Violence
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/domestic-family-violence/defending-women-charged-with-domestic-violence/

Defending women accused of family violence in Houston and Fort Bend County.

Women are increasingly arrested in family violence incidents, sometimes when both parties had injuries or when they acted to defend themselves. Officers responding to a chaotic scene often make quick judgments about who was the primary aggressor.

We examine the history of the relationship, prior incidents, defensive injuries, and self-defense. We also address the practical concerns many of our clients face, such as caregiving responsibilities, custody, and employment.

---

## Domestic Violence FAQ
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/domestic-family-violence/domestic-violence-faqs/

Frequently asked questions about family violence charges in Harris and Fort Bend County.

Here are answers to questions clients often ask after a family violence arrest in Houston, Sugar Land, Richmond or Katy.

Q: Can my partner drop the charges?
A: No. Only the prosecutor can dismiss the case, although the complaining witness's wishes can influence the decision.

Q: Can I go home after I bond out?
A: Not if an emergency protective order or bond condition prohibits it. We can ask the court to modify those conditions.

Q: Will I lose my right to own guns?
A: A family violence conviction triggers a federal firearm prohibition, and Texas law separately restricts possession for five years after a misdemeanor family violence conviction.

Q: Can a family violence case be sealed?
A: If the case is dismissed or you are acquitted, you may qualify for expunction. Deferred adjudication with a family violence finding generally cannot be sealed.

Q: Should I talk to the police to explain my side?
A: Not without a lawyer. Statements made to explain can easily become evidence for the State.

---

## Expunging a Domestic Violence Arrest
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/domestic-family-violence/expunging-domestic-violence/

When a family violence arrest can be expunged in Texas.

A family violence arrest can be expunged if the case was dismissed under qualifying conditions, no-billed by a grand jury, or ended in acquittal. A conviction cannot be expunged, and deferred adjudication involving family violence is excluded from nondisclosure.

Because the options are limited after a plea, the decisions made while the case is pending matter enormously. See Expunctions & Record Sealing.

---

## Injury to a Child
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/domestic-family-violence/child-abuse-and-injury-to-a-child/

Injury to a child and child abuse charges in Houston and Fort Bend County: penalties and defenses.

Injury to a child under Penal Code § 22.04 covers causing bodily injury, serious bodily injury, or serious mental deficiency to a child 14 or younger, by act or by omission. The offense level depends on the injury and the mental state, ranging from a state jail felony to a first-degree felony.

These cases often involve medical opinions about how an injury occurred, and those opinions can be wrong. Accidental injuries, medical conditions, and reasonable discipline are possible defenses. CPS investigations usually run alongside the criminal case, and we coordinate both.

---

## Injury to an Elderly or Disabled Person
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/domestic-family-violence/injury-to-elderly-or-disabled-individual/

Injury to an elderly or disabled individual charges in Texas.

Section 22.04 also protects people 65 and older and people with disabilities. Charges often involve caregivers, family members, and healthcare workers, and they may be based on an omission, such as failing to provide care, as well as an act.

The State must prove the person had a legal duty to act and that the injury resulted from the conduct alleged. Medical records and care history are central to the defense.

---

## Elder Neglect
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/domestic-family-violence/elder-neglect/

Elder neglect charges against family members and caregivers in Harris and Fort Bend County.

Neglect cases usually arise when an elderly person is found in poor health or living conditions. Prosecutors must show the accused had a legal duty, such as a statutory, contractual, or assumed caregiving responsibility, and failed to meet it in a way that caused injury.

Many families are doing their best with limited resources and a loved one who refuses help. We gather medical, financial, and care records to show the full picture, and we coordinate with any Adult Protective Services investigation.

---

## Abandoning or Endangering a Child
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/domestic-family-violence/abandoning-or-endangering-a-child/

Child endangerment and abandonment charges in Texas: penalties and defenses.

Endangering a child means intentionally, knowingly, recklessly, or with criminal negligence placing a child younger than 15 in imminent danger of death, bodily injury, or physical or mental impairment. It is generally a state jail felony. Abandonment is leaving a child under 15 in any place without reasonable and necessary care, and ranges from a state jail felony to a second-degree felony.

These charges are sometimes filed alongside DWI or drug cases when a child is present. The danger must be imminent, not speculative.

---

## Houston & Fort Bend Sex Crimes Defense Lawyer
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/sex-crimes/

Confidential sex crime defense in Houston and Fort Bend County: sexual assault, indecency, online solicitation, prostitution and registration issues.

An accusation of a sexual offense can upend your life before any evidence is tested. Many of these offenses carry long prison ranges and sex-offender registration under Chapter 62 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, which can last ten years or a lifetime and restricts where you live and work.

These investigations often begin quietly with a forensic interview, a sexual assault exam, or a request that you "come in and give your side." Do not speak with investigators before talking to a lawyer. Early representation can shape whether charges are filed at all.

We handle these cases with discretion. We examine forensic interviews and medical findings, recover digital evidence, investigate motives and timelines, and retain qualified experts. Every client is presumed innocent, and we defend every case as if it is going to trial.

---

## Sexual Assault
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/sex-crimes/sexual-assault/

Sexual assault and aggravated sexual assault charges in Harris and Fort Bend County: penalties and defenses.

Sexual assault under Penal Code § 22.011 involves sexual contact or penetration without consent, as defined by statute. It is a second-degree felony. Aggravated sexual assault under § 22.021, which involves serious bodily injury, threats, weapons, drugs, multiple actors, or certain victims, is a first-degree felony.

Consent, identity, and credibility are the most common issues. We review the timeline of reports, text and social-media communications, SANE examination findings, DNA results, and witness accounts. Conviction requires registration as a sex offender.

---

## Sexual Assault of a Child
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/sex-crimes/sexual-assault-of-a-child/

Sexual assault of a child charges in Texas: penalties, registration and defenses.

Sexual contact with a person under 17 is charged as sexual assault of a child, a second-degree felony, regardless of consent. If the child is under 14, the offense is aggravated sexual assault of a child, a first-degree felony with a 25-year minimum sentence.

These cases often rest on a child's statements in a forensic interview at a children's advocacy center. Interview techniques, delayed outcry, outside influences, and inconsistent accounts are critical areas of investigation. We work with forensic psychologists and other experts when needed.

---

## Statutory Rape
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/sex-crimes/statutory-rape/

Statutory rape in Texas: age of consent, the close-in-age defense and penalties.

Texas does not use the term "statutory rape," but the age of consent is 17. Sexual activity with a person younger than 17 is prosecuted as sexual assault of a child even if the minor agreed.

There is a limited close-in-age affirmative defense when the accused was no more than three years older, the minor was at least 14, and the accused was not a registered sex offender. Other restrictions apply. Many of these cases involve young people in relationships, and early intervention can make a significant difference.

---

## Indecency With a Child
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/sex-crimes/indecency-with-a-child/

Indecency with a child by contact or exposure: Texas penalties and defenses.

Indecency with a child involves sexual contact with, or exposure to, a child younger than 17. Indecency by contact is a second-degree felony; indecency by exposure is a third-degree felony. Both generally require sex-offender registration upon conviction or deferred adjudication.

The State must prove specific intent to arouse or gratify sexual desire. Accidental or innocent contact, such as during caregiving or play, is not a crime. These cases are highly fact-specific and require thorough investigation.

---

## Indecent Assault
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/sex-crimes/indecent-assault/

Indecent assault charges in Texas: Class A misdemeanor offense created in 2019.

Indecent assault, created in 2019, involves touching or exposure for a sexual purpose without consent, such as touching intimate areas or causing someone to contact bodily fluids. It is a Class A misdemeanor.

Although it is a misdemeanor, a conviction can carry significant collateral consequences. Consent, intent, and identity are frequent defense issues.

---

## Indecent Exposure
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/sex-crimes/indecent-exposure/

Indecent exposure charges in Houston and Fort Bend County: penalties and registration risks.

Indecent exposure means exposing one's genitals with intent to arouse or gratify sexual desire, while recklessly disregarding whether another person who would be offended or alarmed is present. It is a Class B misdemeanor. A second conviction can trigger sex-offender registration.

Urinating in public, wardrobe malfunctions, and similar situations lack the required intent. We fight to keep these charges from becoming permanent records.

---

## Public Lewdness
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/sex-crimes/public-lewdness/

Public lewdness charges in Texas: Class A misdemeanor defense.

Public lewdness involves certain sexual acts in a public place, or in any place where the actor is reckless about whether another person is present who would be offended. It is a Class A misdemeanor.

Many of these cases come from undercover operations in parks, spas, and similar locations. Entrapment, identity, and whether the location qualifies as public are common issues.

---

## Online Solicitation of a Minor
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/sex-crimes/online-solicitation-of-a-minor/

Online solicitation of a minor charges and sting operations in Houston and Fort Bend County.

Online solicitation of a minor under Penal Code § 33.021 involves communicating online with a person believed to be a minor with the intent to commit a sexual offense, or soliciting a meeting for that purpose. Depending on the conduct and the age involved, it is a third- or second-degree felony.

Many cases come from undercover sting operations in which an adult officer poses as a teenager. We analyze the full chat history, who initiated sexual topics, age representations, and whether law enforcement induced conduct the person was not otherwise disposed to commit.

---

## Child Pornography Possession
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/sex-crimes/child-pornography/

Possession of child sexual abuse material charges: state and federal defense in Houston.

Possessing or accessing visual material depicting a child engaged in sexual conduct is a serious felony under Texas law, with higher ranges for larger amounts, very young children, and repeat offenses. Federal prosecutors also bring these cases, often with mandatory minimum sentences.

These investigations typically begin with a cybertip or peer-to-peer monitoring and lead to a search warrant for devices. Key issues include who had access to the device, whether files were knowingly possessed, how files were downloaded, and the reliability of forensic tools. We work with independent digital forensic examiners.

---

## Promotion of Child Pornography
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/sex-crimes/promotion-of-child-pornography/

Promotion and distribution charges involving child sexual abuse material in Texas.

Promoting, distributing, or possessing with intent to promote such material is punished more severely than possession, and it is commonly alleged when files are found in shared folders on peer-to-peer networks.

Automatic file sharing does not always prove knowing promotion. Forensic analysis of software settings and user activity is critical. These cases often have parallel federal exposure.

---

## Invasive Visual Recording
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/sex-crimes/invasive-visual-recording/

Invasive visual recording charges in Texas: state jail felony penalties and defenses.

Invasive visual recording involves photographing or recording another person's intimate areas without consent, under circumstances where the person had a reasonable expectation of privacy, or recording in a bathroom or changing room. It is a state jail felony.

Defenses focus on intent, consent, and whether the setting carried a reasonable expectation of privacy.

---

## Unlawful Disclosure of Intimate Material
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/sex-crimes/unlawful-disclosure-or-promotion-of-intimate-material-revenge-porn/

Revenge porn and unlawful disclosure of intimate visual material charges in Texas.

Texas prohibits disclosing intimate visual material of another person without consent when the material was obtained or created under circumstances in which the person expected it to remain private, and when disclosure causes harm and reveals the person's identity. It is a state jail felony. Threatening to disclose such material can also be a crime.

These cases often grow out of breakups and involve questions about consent, who posted the material, and account security.

---

## Improper Educator-Student Relationship
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/sex-crimes/improper-relationship-between-educator-and-student/

Improper relationship between educator and student charges in Texas.

An employee of a primary or secondary school who engages in sexual contact with a student enrolled in the same district, or with a student they know is enrolled elsewhere and participating in a school activity, commits a second-degree felony, even if the student is an adult.

These charges also bring licensing and employment consequences through the State Board for Educator Certification. Early representation helps manage both.

---

## Prostitution & Solicitation
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/sex-crimes/prostitution/

Prostitution and solicitation of prostitution charges in Houston: penalties after the 2021 law change.

Since 2021, Texas has treated buyers more harshly than sellers. Selling sexual conduct is generally a Class B misdemeanor, while soliciting prostitution (buying) is a state jail felony, even for a first offense. Penalties increase with prior convictions or if the person solicited is a minor.

Many arrests come from undercover stings, including online ads. Entrapment, the specific words exchanged, and identification are common defenses.

---

## Sexually Oriented Business Violations
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/sex-crimes/sexually-oriented-businesses/

Criminal charges involving sexually oriented businesses in Houston and Harris County.

Houston and Harris County regulate sexually oriented businesses through licensing, location, and conduct rules. Owners, managers, and employees can face criminal charges for operating without a permit, violating conduct regulations, or employing minors.

These cases often involve administrative and criminal components. We defend individuals and businesses and help them address regulatory issues to avoid future charges.

---

## Houston & Fort Bend Theft & Property Crimes Lawyer
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/theft-property-crimes/

Houston and Fort Bend County theft lawyer: shoplifting, burglary, auto theft, fraud, forgery and embezzlement defense.

Theft is considered a crime of "moral turpitude," which means even a misdemeanor conviction can cost someone a job, a professional license, or an immigration benefit. Employers and landlords treat theft convictions as red flags for honesty.

Texas consolidates most property offenses into a single theft statute, Penal Code § 31.03, and grades the offense mainly by the value of the property. Prior theft convictions and certain victims, such as elderly people, can raise the level.

Many first-time theft cases in Harris and Fort Bend Counties qualify for pretrial intervention, which can lead to dismissal and expunction. We also evaluate value, ownership, and intent defenses and, where appropriate, restitution-based resolutions.

---

## Shoplifting
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/theft-property-crimes/shoplifting/

Shoplifting charges at Houston-area stores and malls: penalties, civil demand letters and diversion.

Shoplifting is charged as theft, and the value of the merchandise determines the level. Most cases involve items under $750, a Class B or Class C misdemeanor, but a theft conviction still has serious long-term consequences.

Retailers at the Galleria, Memorial City, First Colony Mall and other locations often rely on loss-prevention video and staff testimony. Mistakes happen, especially with self-checkout lanes and items carried between departments. Retailers may also send a civil demand letter seeking money; that is separate from the criminal case. Diversion programs are often available for first-time cases.

---

## Self-Checkout Theft
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/theft-property-crimes/self-checkout-theft/

Self-checkout theft accusations in Houston and Fort Bend County: intent and defenses.

Self-checkout lanes have produced a wave of theft accusations involving items that did not scan, were scanned at the wrong price, or were left in a cart. Theft requires intent to deprive the owner of property; an honest mistake with a scanner is not a crime.

We obtain the transaction log, store video, and receipts to show what actually happened. Many of these cases are good candidates for dismissal.

---

## Cite and Release for Theft
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/theft-property-crimes/cite-and-release-theft-tickets/

Theft citations instead of arrest in Texas: what a cite-and-release theft ticket means.

For some low-level theft offenses, Texas law allows officers to issue a citation instead of making an arrest, depending on local policy. A citation is still a criminal charge, and failing to appear can lead to a warrant.

Treat a theft citation as seriously as an arrest. We can often resolve these cases through dismissal or deferred disposition that keeps the record eligible for expunction.

---

## Burglary
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/theft-property-crimes/burglary/

Burglary of a habitation, building and vehicle charges in Houston and Fort Bend County.

Burglary is entering a building or habitation without consent with intent to commit a felony, theft, or assault, or committing one of those offenses after entering. Burglary of a vehicle is a separate offense.

## Penalty Levels
Burglary of a building is a state jail felony; burglary of a habitation is a second-degree felony, and a first-degree felony if the intended offense was another felony other than theft. Burglary of a vehicle is a Class A misdemeanor, with enhancements for prior convictions.

Intent at the time of entry is often contested, as is identification from video or fingerprints. Our affiliated family firm has obtained dismissal of a combined burglary and family violence case.

---

## Auto Theft
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/theft-property-crimes/auto-theft/

Unauthorized use of a vehicle and auto theft charges in Texas.

Taking a vehicle can be charged as theft, based on the vehicle's value, or as unauthorized use of a motor vehicle, a state jail felony that does not require intent to permanently deprive the owner.

Many cases involve borrowed cars, disputes over ownership or payments, and rideshare or rental situations. Consent and ownership are frequently contested.

---

## Receiving Stolen Property
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/theft-property-crimes/receiving-stolen-property/

Possession of stolen property charges in Texas: knowledge and defenses.

Texas prosecutes receiving stolen property as theft. The State must prove you knew the property was stolen. Buying something at a low price or from an informal seller does not by itself prove knowledge.

Pawn shop, online marketplace, and resale cases often turn on what the buyer was told and what they reasonably believed.

---

## Employee Theft
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/theft-property-crimes/employee-theft/

Employee theft and internal theft accusations in Houston businesses.

Employers often discover alleged employee theft through audits, inventory shrinkage, or video. Some confront the employee and request a written statement before calling police. Do not sign anything without legal advice.

Many workplace theft allegations are civil or contractual disputes over commissions, reimbursements, or authority. We push back on premature criminal referrals and, where appropriate, negotiate resolutions that avoid prosecution.

---

## Theft by Check
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/theft-property-crimes/theft-by-check/

Theft by check and issuance of a bad check charges in Texas.

Writing a check that bounces can lead to two different charges. Issuance of a bad check is a Class C misdemeanor. Theft by check, which requires proof that the check was used to obtain property with intent to deprive, is graded by value like other theft.

The law presumes intent in certain circumstances, but that presumption can be rebutted. Many cases resolve through restitution and dismissal.

---

## Theft of Service
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/theft-property-crimes/theft-of-service/

Theft of service charges in Texas: unpaid services, rentals and contractors.

Theft of service involves obtaining services, such as hotel stays, restaurant meals, rentals, or contractor work, with intent to avoid payment. It is graded by value like theft.

Disputes over quality of work or billing are not crimes. We distinguish civil disagreements from criminal intent and seek dismissal where the facts support it.

---

## Credit & Debit Card Abuse
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/theft-property-crimes/credit-debit-card-abuse/

Credit card abuse and fraudulent use of identifying information charges in Houston.

Credit or debit card abuse, such as using a card without the owner's consent, is a state jail felony. Fraudulent use or possession of identifying information is graded by the number of items involved and can reach a first-degree felony.

Many cases involve family members or roommates who believed they had permission. Video, IP and device data, and delivery records are central to the evidence.

---

## Criminal Mischief
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/theft-property-crimes/criminal-mischief/

Criminal mischief and vandalism charges in Texas: penalties by damage amount.

Criminal mischief means intentionally or knowingly damaging, destroying, or tampering with someone else's property without consent. Like theft, it is graded by the amount of loss, from a Class C misdemeanor to a first-degree felony.

Many cases arise from heated disputes between partners or neighbors. Ownership, consent, and the actual cost of repair are often disputed.

---

## Criminal Trespass
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/theft-property-crimes/criminal-trespass/

Criminal trespass charges in Houston and Fort Bend County: notice and defenses.

Criminal trespass is entering or remaining on property without consent after receiving notice that entry was forbidden. Notice can be oral or written, or given by fencing, signs, or purple paint marks. It is usually a Class B misdemeanor, and a Class A misdemeanor in a habitation or with a deadly weapon.

Lack of proper notice and a good-faith belief that you were allowed to be there are common defenses.

---

## Misapplication of Fiduciary Property
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/theft-property-crimes/misapplication-of-fiduciary-property/

Misapplication of fiduciary property charges against trustees, agents and contractors in Texas.

A fiduciary, such as a trustee, executor, attorney-in-fact, or a contractor holding construction trust funds, can be charged with misapplying property in a way that risks loss to the owner. The offense is graded by value.

These cases often begin as family disputes over estates or as business disputes. Authorization, documentation, and good faith are central defenses.

---

## Securing Execution of a Document by Deception
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/theft-property-crimes/sedd/

Securing execution of a document by deception charges in Texas.

This offense involves deceiving someone into signing or executing a document that affects property, services, or someone's financial interests. It is graded by the value involved.

Contract disputes are often recast as criminal deception. We examine what was represented, what the parties understood, and whether a civil remedy is the appropriate path.

---

## Fraud & Forgery
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/theft-property-crimes/fraud-forgery/

Fraud and forgery defense in Houston and Fort Bend County: embezzlement, insurance fraud, forgery and tampering charges.

Fraud and forgery charges usually involve documents, financial records, and digital evidence, and they often follow months of investigation. Getting a lawyer involved before charges are filed can make the difference between a civil resolution and a criminal case.

See also our White-Collar & Fraud practice for investigations involving businesses, securities, and federal agencies.

---

## Embezzlement
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/theft-property-crimes/fraud-forgery/embezzlement/

Embezzlement charges in Houston: theft by employees, officers and fiduciaries.

Texas prosecutes embezzlement as theft or misapplication of fiduciary property, graded by the total amount. Because separate takings can be aggregated into one charge, small amounts over time can become a serious felony.

We work with forensic accountants to test the State's calculations, identify authorized transactions, and evaluate restitution-based resolutions.

---

## Forgery
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/theft-property-crimes/fraud-forgery/forgery-of-a-financial-instrument/

Forgery of checks and financial instruments in Texas: penalties and defenses.

Forgery is altering, making, completing, or passing a writing with intent to defraud or harm. Forging a check or other financial instrument is a state jail felony; forging government records or money is more serious.

The State must prove intent to defraud and that you knew the document was forged. Passing a check someone else forged, without knowledge, is not forgery.

---

## False Statement to Obtain Credit
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/theft-property-crimes/fraud-forgery/false-statement-to-obtain-credit/

False statement to obtain property or credit charges in Texas.

Knowingly making a materially false statement to obtain property or credit, including loans and mortgages, is graded by value. These cases frequently overlap with federal bank and mortgage fraud.

Loan applications are often completed by brokers or loan officers. Who prepared the information, and whether the statement was material to the lender's decision, are central questions.

---

## Insurance Fraud
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/theft-property-crimes/fraud-forgery/insurance-fraud/

Insurance fraud charges in Texas: auto, property and health claims.

Insurance fraud involves presenting a statement in support of a claim that the person knows is false and material. It is graded by the value of the claim.

Insurers' special investigation units often refer cases to prosecutors after denying a claim. Disagreements about the extent of damage or loss are not fraud. We examine the claim file and communications closely.

---

## Online Impersonation
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/theft-property-crimes/fraud-forgery/online-impersonation/

Online impersonation charges in Texas: fake profiles and messages.

Using another person's name or persona to create a web page or post messages on social media without consent, with intent to harm, defraud, intimidate, or threaten, is a third-degree felony. Sending messages that falsely appear to come from someone else is a lesser offense.

Attribution is the key issue: proving who actually created the account and sent the messages.

---

## Tampering With Evidence
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/theft-property-crimes/fraud-forgery/tampering-with-evidence/

Tampering with or fabricating physical evidence charges in Texas.

Tampering with evidence means altering, destroying, or concealing something with intent to impair its availability as evidence, knowing an investigation is pending or in progress. It is generally a third-degree felony.

These charges are often added when someone discards an item during a police encounter. The State must prove the specific intent and knowledge required by the statute.

---

## Tampering With Government Records
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/theft-property-crimes/fraud-forgery/tampering-with-government-records/

Tampering with a governmental record charges in Texas, including temporary tags.

Tampering with a governmental record includes making false entries in, altering, or using a false government record, such as a driver's license, temporary vehicle tag, or official document. Penalties range from a Class A misdemeanor to a felony depending on the record and intent.

Counterfeit temporary paper tags have been a particular enforcement focus in the Houston area.

---

## Houston White-Collar Crime Defense Lawyer
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/white-collar-crimes/

Houston white-collar crime defense lawyer: fraud, embezzlement, securities, health care fraud, money laundering and federal investigations.

White-collar cases are won with documents, preparation, and early strategy. Many begin with a subpoena, a target letter, a search warrant, or an agent's unannounced visit. What you say and produce in those first days can shape everything that follows.

Ishmael G. A. Pink brings a combined litigation and transactional background to these cases. Having advised startups and privately held companies on SaaS agreements, B2B disputes, and securities matters, he understands how businesses actually operate, which is often the key to explaining conduct that investigators have misread.

## How We Help
- Respond to subpoenas, target letters, and agent contacts.
- Conduct internal reviews with forensic accountants.
- Present information to prosecutors before charges are filed.
- Defend state cases in Harris and Fort Bend Counties and federal cases in the Southern District of Texas.
- Coordinate parallel civil litigation and regulatory proceedings.

---

## Securities Fraud
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/white-collar-crimes/securities-fraud/

Securities fraud investigations and charges in Houston: state and federal defense.

Securities fraud can be charged under the Texas Securities Act and under federal law, and it often runs alongside SEC or Texas State Securities Board investigations. Issues include misrepresentations to investors, unregistered offerings, and acting as an unregistered dealer or advisor.

Startups and private companies are especially exposed when fundraising documents are informal. We analyze offering materials, investor communications, and the intent behind them, and we coordinate the criminal defense with any regulatory matter.

---

## Health Care Fraud
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/white-collar-crimes/health-care-fraud/

Health care and Medicaid fraud defense in Houston: billing, kickbacks and medical necessity.

Houston is a national focus for health care fraud enforcement. Cases involve billing for services not rendered, upcoding, medical necessity disputes, and kickback allegations under federal and Texas law.

Many cases rest on complex billing rules that honest providers struggle to apply. We work with billing and coding experts to show good faith and challenge the government's loss calculations.

---

## Money Laundering
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/white-collar-crimes/money-laundering/

Money laundering charges in Texas and federal court.

Money laundering involves knowingly conducting financial transactions with proceeds of criminal activity. Texas grades it by amount, from a state jail felony to a first-degree felony, and federal law imposes up to 20 years.

The government must prove knowledge that the funds came from crime. Business owners and family members are sometimes accused based on transactions they did not understand.

---

## Wire & Mail Fraud
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/white-collar-crimes/wire-and-mail-fraud/

Federal wire fraud and mail fraud defense in the Southern District of Texas.

Wire fraud and mail fraud are the federal government's most common fraud charges, covering any scheme to defraud that uses interstate wires or the mail. Each email or transfer can be a separate count, each carrying up to 20 years.

The core question is intent to defraud. Business failures, optimistic projections, and contract disputes are not crimes. We use the documents to tell the full story.

---

## Bank & Loan Fraud
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/white-collar-crimes/bank-and-mortgage-fraud/

Bank fraud, PPP loan fraud and mortgage fraud defense in Houston.

Bank and loan fraud investigations, including those involving pandemic-era PPP and EIDL loans, remain active. Federal bank fraud carries up to 30 years, and the statute of limitations can be long.

Many borrowers relied on preparers or lenders who completed applications for them. We examine who supplied the information, what the borrower understood, and how the funds were used.

---

## Houston & Fort Bend Weapons Charge Lawyer
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/weapon-firearm-charges/

Houston and Fort Bend County gun charge lawyer: unlawful carrying, felon in possession, prohibited places and deadly conduct.

Since September 2021, most Texans 21 and older who are not otherwise prohibited can carry a handgun without a license. That change did not end weapons prosecutions. It shifted them toward questions about who is prohibited, where a weapon was carried, and how it was displayed or used.

Houston-area weapons cases commonly arise from traffic stops, bar and nightlife incidents, road-rage encounters, and searches incident to other arrests. A weapons conviction can also cost you the right to possess firearms, a License to Carry, and certain jobs. We test the stop, the search, the prohibited-person status, and the location element in every case.

---

## Unlawfully Carrying a Weapon
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/weapon-firearm-charges/unlawfully-carrying-a-weapon/

Unlawful carrying of a weapon charges in Texas after permitless carry: who is prohibited and the penalties.

Unlawfully carrying a weapon under Penal Code § 46.02 still applies to people younger than 21 (with limited exceptions), people prohibited from possessing firearms, people engaged in criminal activity other than a Class C traffic offense, people who are members of a criminal street gang, and people carrying on premises licensed to sell alcohol. It is generally a Class A misdemeanor, and a third-degree felony on alcohol-licensed premises.

People convicted of unlawful carrying before permitless carry took effect may qualify to have that record expunged. See Expunging Unlawful Carrying.

---

## Places Weapons Are Prohibited
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/weapon-firearm-charges/places-weapons-are-prohibited/

Where guns are prohibited in Texas: schools, courts, polling places, airports and posted businesses.

Penal Code §§ 46.03 and 46.035 list places where weapons are prohibited, including schools and school events, polling places on election day, courts and court offices, racetracks, secured areas of airports such as Bush Intercontinental and Hobby, and certain other locations. Many of these violations are third-degree felonies.

Private businesses can also prohibit carry through properly worded signs under §§ 30.06 and 30.07. Signs that do not meet the statutory requirements may not provide effective notice. Airport checkpoint cases are common, and many can be resolved without a conviction.

---

## Felon in Possession of a Firearm
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/weapon-firearm-charges/possession-of-a-weapon-by-a-felon/

Unlawful possession of a firearm by a felon: Texas and federal charges in Houston.

Under Penal Code § 46.04, a person convicted of a felony cannot possess a firearm until five years after release from confinement or supervision, whichever is later, and after that only at their home. A violation is a third-degree felony. People convicted of misdemeanor family violence are prohibited for five years after supervision ends.

Federal law, 18 U.S.C. § 922(g), imposes a separate and broader prohibition, and federal prosecutors in Houston frequently adopt these cases. We examine the prior conviction, the timing, knowledge of possession, and the legality of the search.

---

## Firearms at Bars & 51% Establishments
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/weapon-firearm-charges/firearm-possession-at-a-bar-or-alcohol-establishment/

Carrying a gun in a bar or 51% establishment in Texas: felony penalties and defenses.

Carrying a handgun on premises that earn 51 percent or more of their income from on-site alcohol sales is a third-degree felony, whether or not the person has a License to Carry. Those businesses must post a red "51%" sign.

Whether the business actually qualified, whether proper signage was displayed, and whether the person knew where they were are all legitimate defense issues. Carrying while intoxicated carries separate consequences.

---

## Deadly Conduct With a Firearm
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/weapon-firearm-charges/deadly-conduct-with-a-firearm/

Deadly conduct with a firearm charges in Houston: pointing or discharging a gun.

Pointing a firearm at someone, whether or not it is loaded, is presumed to be reckless deadly conduct, a Class A misdemeanor. Knowingly discharging a firearm at or in the direction of people, a house, a building, or a vehicle is a third-degree felony.

Self-defense and defense of property often apply. Texas law justifies the threat of deadly force in situations where deadly force itself would be justified, and creating the apprehension of force is treated differently than using it.

---

## Discharging a Firearm in City Limits
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/weapon-firearm-charges/discharge-of-firearm-in-certain-municipalities/

Discharge of a firearm in certain municipalities in Texas, including Houston.

Recklessly discharging a firearm inside the limits of a municipality with a population of 100,000 or more, such as Houston, is a Class A misdemeanor under Penal Code § 42.12. Many other cities have local ordinances restricting discharge.

Celebratory gunfire on holidays leads to many of these charges. Defenses include self-defense, lawful hunting or range use, and lack of recklessness.

---

## Making a Firearm Accessible to a Child
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/weapon-firearm-charges/making-a-firearm-accessible-to-a-child/

Making a firearm accessible to a child charges in Texas.

Texas law makes it an offense to leave a readily dischargeable firearm where a child younger than 17 could access it, when the child does access it. It is a Class C misdemeanor, and a Class A misdemeanor if the child discharges the firearm and causes death or serious bodily injury.

Defenses include that the firearm was secured with a locking device or stored in a locked place, or that the child gained access through unlawful entry. These cases are often tragic accidents and call for careful, compassionate handling.

---

## Taking a Peace Officer's Weapon
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/weapon-firearm-charges/taking-a-peace-officers-firearm/

Taking or attempting to take a peace officer's weapon charges in Texas.

Intentionally or knowingly taking or attempting to take a firearm, nightstick, stun gun, or similar device from a peace officer who is performing official duties is a state jail felony, and more serious if the weapon is fired or someone is injured.

These charges usually arise from struggles during arrest. Body-camera video is crucial to show whether the contact was intentional or incidental.

---

## Road Rage Incidents With a Weapon
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/weapon-firearm-charges/road-rage-incidents-with-weapon-possession-in-texas/

Road rage gun charges on Houston highways: deadly conduct, aggravated assault and self-defense.

Confrontations on I-610, I-45, the Beltway and the Grand Parkway too often involve firearms. Charges can range from disorderly conduct for displaying a weapon, to deadly conduct for pointing it, to aggravated assault with a deadly weapon.

What matters most is what each driver did and reasonably believed. Dash-camera footage, traffic cameras, 911 calls, and independent witnesses often tell a different story than the first report. Self-defense is frequently a strong defense in these cases.

---

## Houston Federal Criminal Defense Lawyer
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/federal-crimes/

Houston federal criminal defense lawyer: drug conspiracy, firearms, fraud and investigations in the Southern District of Texas.

Federal cases in Houston are prosecuted by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Texas and heard at the Bob Casey U.S. Courthouse downtown. Federal investigations by the FBI, DEA, ATF, HSI, IRS-CI, and the Postal Inspection Service are typically long and thorough, and by the time charges are filed, the government has built its case.

Augustin T. Pink has obtained dismissals, jury acquittals, and sentence reductions in federal court over a career that began in 1992. We engage early, evaluate the discovery and the Sentencing Guidelines exposure, litigate suppression issues, and prepare every case for trial.

---

## Federal Investigations & Target Letters
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/federal-crimes/federal-investigations-target-letters/

What to do if you receive a federal target letter, grand jury subpoena, or visit from federal agents in Houston.

A target letter means federal prosecutors consider you a likely defendant. A grand jury subpoena or a visit from agents may mean you are a witness, a subject, or a target. In every case, it is time to speak with a lawyer before you speak with the government.

Early representation can allow us to present information that changes the government's view, negotiate the terms of any interview, protect privileged documents, and in some cases avoid charges entirely.

---

## Federal Drug Conspiracy
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/federal-crimes/federal-drug-conspiracy/

Federal drug conspiracy and trafficking defense in Houston: mandatory minimums and safety valve.

Federal drug charges under 21 U.S.C. §§ 841 and 846 often carry mandatory minimum sentences of five or ten years depending on the drug and quantity. In a conspiracy, the government may try to hold each person responsible for quantities attributed to the entire group.

Defenses include challenging wiretaps and searches, contesting membership in the conspiracy, disputing drug quantity, and seeking relief under the safety-valve provision, which can allow a sentence below the mandatory minimum for qualifying defendants.

---

## Federal Firearm Charges
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/federal-crimes/federal-firearm-charges/

Federal gun charges in the Southern District of Texas: felon in possession, 924(c) and straw purchases.

Common federal firearm charges include possession by a prohibited person under 18 U.S.C. § 922(g), using or carrying a firearm during a drug trafficking crime or crime of violence under § 924(c), which carries consecutive mandatory minimums, and false statements in firearm purchases (straw purchases).

Many federal gun cases begin as state arrests by HPD or the Harris County Sheriff's Office and are later adopted federally. We evaluate the search, knowledge of possession, and constitutional challenges that continue to develop in the courts.

---

## Federal Sentencing
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/federal-crimes/federal-sentencing/

How federal sentencing works: the Sentencing Guidelines, departures, variances and mitigation.

Federal sentences are calculated under the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines, which assign an offense level and criminal history category. The Guidelines are advisory, and judges must consider the factors in 18 U.S.C. § 3553(a), including the person's history and characteristics.

Effective sentencing advocacy starts long before the hearing. We challenge Guideline enhancements, prepare a detailed mitigation presentation, and address objections to the presentence report. Our family of firms has obtained significant federal sentence reductions.

---

## Federal Fraud Charges
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/federal-crimes/federal-fraud/

Federal fraud defense in Houston: wire, mail, bank, health care and securities fraud.

Federal fraud charges include wire and mail fraud, bank and loan fraud, health care fraud, securities fraud, and conspiracy. Loss amount drives much of the Sentencing Guidelines calculation, so the government's loss figure is often the most important number in the case.

See our White-Collar & Fraud practice for more detail on these investigations.

## Houston & Fort Bend Serious Traffic Offense Lawyer
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/serious-traffic-offenses/

Houston and Fort Bend County serious traffic offense lawyer: failure to stop and render aid, evading in a vehicle, racing, reckless driving and suspended license.

Some traffic cases are far more than tickets. Leaving the scene of a crash, evading police in a vehicle, street racing, and driving while your license is invalid can lead to jail, felony records, and long license suspensions.

Houston's roads, from the Southwest Freeway to the Grand Parkway, see heavy enforcement by HPD, the Harris County Sheriff's Office, constables, Fort Bend County deputies, and DPS. We obtain dash-camera and body-camera footage, crash reports, and vehicle data to build a defense.

---

## Failure to Stop and Render Aid
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/serious-traffic-offenses/failing-to-stop/

Failure to stop and render aid (hit and run) charges in Houston and Fort Bend County.

A driver involved in a crash that results in injury or death must stop, return to the scene, give their information, and render reasonable assistance. Failing to do so is a felony under Transportation Code § 550.021, with the most serious penalties when a death results.

The State must prove the driver knew a crash occurred and knew or should have known someone was injured. Darkness, weather, panic, and fear for one's own safety are relevant to that question.

---

## Leaving the Scene: Injury or Death
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/serious-traffic-offenses/failing-to-stop/injury-or-death/

Felony leaving the scene of an accident involving injury or death in Texas.

When a crash causes serious bodily injury or death and a driver leaves, prosecutors pursue felony charges and often seek prison time. These cases also bring civil liability, and the person may face separate intoxication or manslaughter charges.

We reconstruct the timeline and investigate what the driver actually perceived. In some cases, the driver did stop or return, or the information given satisfied the statute.

---

## Leaving the Scene: Vehicle Damage
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/serious-traffic-offenses/accidents-involving-vehicles/

Leaving the scene of an accident with vehicle damage in Texas: misdemeanor penalties.

When a crash damages only an attended vehicle, the driver must stop and exchange information. Failing to do so is a Class C misdemeanor if the damage is under $200 and a Class B misdemeanor if it is $200 or more.

Disputes over the amount of damage, whether the driver knew contact occurred, and whether information was exchanged are common defense issues.

---

## Striking an Unattended Vehicle
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/serious-traffic-offenses/duty-on-striking-unattended-vehicle/

Duty on striking an unattended vehicle in Texas: notice requirements and penalties.

A driver who hits an unattended vehicle must stop and either locate the owner or leave a written note with their name and address. Failing to do so is a Class C misdemeanor for damage under $200 and a Class B misdemeanor for damage of $200 or more.

---

## Striking a Fixture or Highway Landscaping
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/serious-traffic-offenses/duty-on-striking-fixture/

Duty on striking a fixture or highway landscaping in Texas.

Drivers who damage fixtures, signs, fences, or landscaping on or near a highway must take reasonable steps to notify the owner and, in some cases, report to police. Penalties depend on the amount of damage, similar to other leaving-the-scene offenses.

---

## Crashes Involving Injury
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/serious-traffic-offenses/motor-vehicle-accidents-involving-injury/

Criminal exposure after a car crash involving injury in Houston.

A crash that injures someone can lead to criminal charges ranging from failure to stop and render aid, to intoxication assault, to manslaughter, depending on the facts. It also creates civil liability.

If you were involved in a serious crash, speak with a lawyer before giving a recorded statement to police or an insurance company. We coordinate the criminal defense with the insurance and civil issues.

---

## Evading Arrest in a Vehicle
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/serious-traffic-offenses/evading-arrest-in-vehicle/

Evading arrest or detention in a vehicle in Texas: felony penalties and defenses.

Intentionally fleeing in a vehicle from a person you know is a peace officer attempting a lawful arrest or detention is a felony in Texas, and the penalty increases with prior convictions or if someone is seriously injured or killed.

The State must prove you knew an officer was trying to stop you and that the attempted detention was lawful. Delayed pull-overs to find a safe location are not evading.

---

## Street Racing
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/serious-traffic-offenses/racing/

Racing on a highway charges in Houston and Fort Bend County.

Racing on a highway, including drag races, speed competitions, and "takeovers," is a Class B misdemeanor. It becomes a Class A misdemeanor with a prior conviction or open container, a state jail or third-degree felony if someone is injured, and a second-degree felony if someone dies. Vehicles can be seized in some cases.

Houston has increased enforcement against street takeovers. Identification of drivers and proof of an actual race are central issues.

---

## Reckless Driving
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/serious-traffic-offenses/reckless-driving/

Reckless driving charges in Texas: penalties and use as a reduced charge.

Reckless driving is driving in wilful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property. It is a misdemeanor punishable by up to 30 days in jail and a fine of up to $200. It is sometimes negotiated as a reduction from more serious offenses, including DWI.

---

## Driving While License Invalid
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/serious-traffic-offenses/driving-while-license-invalid-or-suspended/

Driving while license invalid or suspended charges in Houston and Fort Bend County.

Driving while your license is suspended or invalid is usually a Class C misdemeanor for a first offense. It becomes a Class B misdemeanor with a prior conviction, if you had no insurance at the time, or if the suspension resulted from certain offenses, and it can become more serious if a crash causes injury.

Many people do not know their license was suspended. We help clients resolve the underlying suspension, obtain an occupational license if needed, and resolve the charge.

---

## Houston Alcohol Offense Lawyer
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/alcohol-offenses/

Underage drinking, minor in possession, fake ID and public intoxication defense in Houston and Fort Bend County.

Alcohol-related offenses are common around Houston's nightlife districts, college campuses, concerts, and sporting events. Most are misdemeanors, but they still create a criminal record and, for minors, can mean license suspensions and school discipline.

Most first-time alcohol offenses can be resolved through deferred disposition, classes, or dismissal, followed by expunction. Handling the case correctly the first time matters, because repeat offenses lose those options.

---

## Public Intoxication
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/alcohol-offenses/public-intoxication/

Public intoxication charges in Houston: Class C penalties and keeping a clean record.

Public intoxication is appearing in a public place while intoxicated to the degree that you may endanger yourself or others. It is a Class C misdemeanor, punishable by a fine. Minors face additional consequences under the Alcoholic Beverage Code.

Officers make these arrests based on judgment calls. We challenge whether the person was actually a danger and pursue dismissal or deferred disposition followed by expunction.

---

## Minor in Possession
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/alcohol-offenses/minor-in-possession/

Minor in possession of alcohol charges in Texas: penalties and expunction.

A person under 21 who possesses alcohol commits a Class C misdemeanor, with exceptions for possession in the presence of a parent, guardian, or spouse who is an adult, and for certain employment. Penalties can include a fine, alcohol awareness classes, community service, and a driver license suspension.

First offenses are often eligible for deferred disposition and later expunction.

---

## Underage Drinking
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/alcohol-offenses/minor-in-possession/underage-drinking/

Underage drinking charges in Houston and Fort Bend County.

Underage drinking charges include possession, consumption, purchase, and driving under the influence by a minor. A third offense can carry jail time and is not eligible for deferred disposition.

Parents should know that these cases can affect scholarships and college admissions. We focus on outcomes that leave no permanent record.

---

## Minor in Consumption
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/alcohol-offenses/minor-in-consumption/

Minor in consumption of alcohol charges in Texas.

Consuming alcohol under 21 is a Class C misdemeanor, with similar exceptions and consequences as possession. The State must prove the person actually consumed alcohol, often through officer observations or admissions.

---

## Furnishing Alcohol to Minors
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/alcohol-offenses/furnishing-alcohol-to-minors/

Furnishing alcohol to a minor charges in Texas: Class A misdemeanor defense.

Purchasing alcohol for or giving alcohol to a person under 21 is a Class A misdemeanor, with an exception for a parent, guardian, or spouse who is visibly present. Making alcohol available at a party can also lead to charges, and to civil liability if someone is hurt.

---

## Misrepresentation of Age
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/alcohol-offenses/misrepresentation-of-age/

Misrepresentation of age by a minor to buy alcohol in Texas.

A minor who falsely states they are 21 or older, or presents false identification, to obtain alcohol commits a Class C misdemeanor. Using a false ID can also lead to more serious charges.

---

## Possession of a Fictitious License
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/alcohol-offenses/possession-of-a-fictitious-license/

Possession of a fictitious or altered driver license in Texas.

Possessing a fictitious, altered, or borrowed driver license or ID card can be charged under the Transportation Code or the Penal Code. Penalties range from a Class C misdemeanor for some underage cases to a Class A misdemeanor or felony for manufacturing or possessing with intent to use.

---

## Possession of a Fake ID
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/alcohol-offenses/possession-of-fake-id/

Fake ID charges in Houston: penalties for students and young adults.

Fake ID charges are common near college campuses and bars. Depending on the facts, prosecutors may charge a Class A misdemeanor under the Transportation Code or a more serious offense for manufacturing or selling.

Because a misdemeanor conviction can affect admissions and employment, we work toward dismissal or reduction and expunction.

---

## Arrests & Police Encounters
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/arrests/

Your rights during an arrest in Houston and Fort Bend County: searches, resisting arrest, evading and failure to identify charges.

What happens during an arrest often decides the outcome of the case. Unlawful stops, searches without consent or a warrant, and statements taken without proper warnings can all lead to evidence being suppressed.

You have the right to remain silent and the right to refuse consent to a search. Exercise those rights politely, do not physically resist, and ask for a lawyer. Then call us at (832) 979-0882.

---

## Searches & Seizures
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/arrests/search-and-seizures/

Illegal search and seizure defenses in Texas criminal cases.

The Fourth Amendment and Article I, Section 9 of the Texas Constitution protect against unreasonable searches and seizures. Police generally need a warrant to search a home or phone. Vehicle searches require probable cause, consent, or another recognized exception.

When police violate these rules, Article 38.23 of the Code of Criminal Procedure requires exclusion of the evidence, and Texas juries can be instructed to disregard illegally obtained evidence. Motions to suppress are among the most powerful tools in a criminal defense.

---

## Resisting Arrest
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/arrests/resisting-arrest/

Resisting arrest, search or transport charges in Houston and Fort Bend County.

Intentionally preventing or obstructing a peace officer from making an arrest, search, or transport by using force against the officer is a Class A misdemeanor, and a third-degree felony if a deadly weapon is used. It is not a defense that the arrest itself was unlawful, but pulling away or going limp may not amount to force against the officer.

---

## Evading Arrest or Detention
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/arrests/evading-arrest-or-detention/

Evading arrest on foot in Texas: penalties and defenses.

Intentionally fleeing from a person you know is a peace officer attempting a lawful arrest or detention is a Class A misdemeanor when on foot. Fleeing in a vehicle is a felony.

If the officer had no lawful basis to detain you, the State cannot prove this offense. Knowledge that the person was an officer is also required.

---

## Fleeing a Police Officer
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/arrests/fleeing-or-eluding/

Fleeing or attempting to elude a police officer under the Texas Transportation Code.

Fleeing or attempting to elude a police officer under Transportation Code § 545.421 involves wilfully failing to stop a vehicle when given a visual or audible signal by a uniformed officer in a marked vehicle. It is generally a Class B misdemeanor, separate from felony evading arrest in a vehicle.

---

## Failure to Identify
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/arrests/failure-to-identify/

Failure to identify and giving false information to police in Texas.

In Texas, you are generally not required to identify yourself to an officer unless you have been lawfully arrested. Refusing to give your name, address, or date of birth after a lawful arrest is a Class C misdemeanor. Giving a false name or information to an officer who has lawfully arrested or detained you is a Class B misdemeanor, and more serious if you are a fugitive.

---

## Interference With Public Duties
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/arrests/interference-with-public-duties/

Interference with public duties charges in Houston: what counts and defenses.

Interfering with a peace officer, emergency medical worker, or firefighter performing duties is a Class B misdemeanor. Speech alone is a defense under the statute, so arguing with or criticizing an officer is not a crime by itself, and recording police from a reasonable distance is generally protected.

---

## Spring Break Arrests
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/arrests/spring-break-arrests/

Spring break arrests in Galveston, South Padre and Texas beach towns: what to do from Houston.

Every spring, students and young adults from Houston are arrested in Galveston, South Padre Island, and other Texas destinations for public intoxication, minor in possession, drug possession, and DWI. Many leave town assuming the case will go away; it will not, and missed court dates lead to warrants.

We can often handle out-of-town cases with minimal travel for the client. See Out-of-County Offenders.

## Houston Student Defense Lawyer
URL: https://www.pinkdefense.com/student-defense/

Criminal defense for college students in Houston: UH, TSU, Rice, HCC and campus disciplinary proceedings.

Houston is home to the University of Houston, Texas Southern University, Rice University, Houston Community College, the University of St. Thomas, Houston Christian University, and many other schools, and Fort Bend County families send students across the state. A criminal case can threaten a student's enrollment, scholarships, financial aid, campus housing, and future licensing.

Many students are eligible for diversion and expunction, which allows them to move forward with a clean record. We also guide students and families through campus conduct processes.
